claim: A. EWC strength provides a controllable stability-plasticity trade-off
evidence: Paired multi-seed forgetting and acquisition changes.

claim: B. The useful lambda region depends on adapter geometry
evidence: Method-specific confirmation grids and Pareto positions.

claim: C. Intermediate regularization can improve balanced memory relative to lambda=0
evidence: Three-seed final mean NLL and paired directions.

claim: D. Very strong EWC reduces forgetting but causes under-learning
evidence: Seed-42 lambda 50/100/300 sweep; not in confirmation grid.

claim: E. Adapter geometries respond differently to identical EWC strength
evidence: Cross-method mean and seed-wise responses at shared lambdas.

claim: F. Parameter-displacement reduction tracks forgetting reduction
evidence: Within-method exploratory correlations; mechanistic consistency, not causality.
